title: Gmktec K8 Gaming Desktop, Dual LAN 2.5gbps $589.60 Delivered @ Amazon DE via Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Gmktec K8 Gaming Desktop, Dual LAN 2.5gbps $589.60 Delivered @ Amazon DE via Amazon AU

[scrimshaw] There have been quite a number of listings for mini PC's on Amazon Global where the specification shown on Amazon.com.au is incorrect. If you go to Amazon.de (Germany) and search for the ASIN B0D1QLQK7G you can see exactly what the model / configuration is supposed to be
https://www.amazon.de/en/dp/B0D1QLQK7G/
A recent example is https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/955133 . The item is no longer in stock, but you can see that the specification is still incorrect to this day.
[dna level c] Thanks for the heads up, I'd love to buy this, but with all the pain the other folks experienced, it's just not worth the risk.
[tunzafun001] Would this be any good for Assetto Corsa Rally, Project cars and similar?
Haven't dabled with any PC "stuff" since 2012 (using a MacBook with a 320M)… So way out of the loop.
Was looking at buying a used laptop with a i7 / GTX 1060 (Alienware 17 R4/ MSI Dominator/ Dell G7 for around $400). Maybe a RTX 2050 option.
Are these little pc things a better option?
No clue on these "gaming specs" outside the intel GeForce environment.
Will just be for racing games and look to store under a couch when not in use.
*Edit - just did some reading..looks like this is rubbish for gaming unless you buy a separate graphics card for it?
P.S. anyone recommend the best budget laptop to play the older racing games?
Cheers
[scrimshaw] I wouldn't be misled by the "Gaming" marketing, it's considered a 'gaming-ready' machine because it has a Radeon 660m iGPU (possibly equal to a mobile GTX 1050, and definitely worse than a GTX 1060 6GB) and secondly, it has an Oculink port.
The Oculink port lets you plug in an external graphics card and basically 'upgrade' the Mini PC into a halfway decent gaming PC. However you not only need to buy a GPU, you also need to buy an Oculink dock. Both of which significantly adds to the total cost of the machine.
[tunzafun001] Cheers mate. I was indeed led astray.
Google AI suggests the dedicated vram GtX 1060 is 200% better than the Radeon 660M.
Looks like an old gaming laptop is still the best choice.
[Frackingiscool] And depending on the card possibly a PSU to power it separately of the box and dock.
[scrimshaw] Yeah that too. Some models like the $259 MINISFORUM Docking Station DEG1 has a power supply built in, but if you go the cheap / hacky route, a PSU is mandatory otherwise you have nothing to plug into the PCIE 6x or 8x
[Frackingiscool] @scrimshaw: I'm a snob. I want to plug an egpu in its own enclosure into the wall and into the unit and my screen into the egpu and the enclosure for my GPU needs to be hefty, mean, look sharp, possibly break a foot or shin if it slipped off the table. None of this folder alloy with all your shit hanging out.
I require Sonnet Breakaway Box 850 T5 eGPU Enclosure – 80 Gbps Thunderbolt 5 / Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 – External GPU for Windows – 850W Power – Triple-Wide Graphics Cards – 5GbE Port https://amzn.asia/d/02tiACgU
And nothing less.
[bboT] @scrimshaw:
MINISFORUM Docking Station DEG1 has a power supply built in
It doesn't. I own 2.
[Frackingiscool] I just got a bosgame "p3plus" ryzen 7840hs 780m igpu, 32gb DDR5, 1tb Kingston NVME drive for $100 more.
Gaming beast, no. Gaming capable, very much yes. All the fallouts, a couple mortal Kombat, some switch emulation, a polite fiddle with the witcher 3 wild hunt.
I'm treating it as a console so controller only (for 90%) of its use outside setup. CachyOS, it's game packages and tweaks, heroic launcher to get all my epic/gog/luna freebies and I'm going great. Enjoying smooth gameplay (from obviously non stressful games) but I'll build up to crysis
[Frackingiscool] Anecdotal, I bought some gaming monitors from Amazon for Christmas presents. 3 monitors I had delivered the week before Xmas as the kids who got them were not going to be home again until after new years.
I went off the description and the photos illustrating the MSI gaming monitors. The generic description and images belonged to the model above. An extra $90 each so I didn't think it was a huge discount and didn't question it.
They opened them, all excited, plugged them in, I went home after giving their parents printouts of the invoice and store page.
2 days later they went to the UK for Christmas, I looked at the invoice and the pictures and noticed the discrepancies.
Got on to Amazon, explained the situation , 3 monitors, wrongly advertised, already delivers and set up and won't have access to return them until the new year if they still have the boxes etc
They refunded me the total amount, said keep them, apologised for the mix up and I noticed my next purchase had a $5 courtesy voucher applied.
Mine was a genuine mistake and I have felt guilty about it since.
Do what you will with this knowledge knowing it can lead down a very dark path of upsetting the Amazonians and ambassadors of the Prime.
